_meta.what: National / PG exams students search for and Shishya had no exam row for (wave 2 search misses). Every fact below was read on the conducting body's own site or its official PDF on that host, with the exact words it came from. Read by scripts/add-national-exams.ts (dry run by default, --apply writes).
_meta.datesAre: Asia/Kolkata calendar dates (YYYY-MM-DD); the script stores them at midnight UTC of that day, the repo-wide convention.
_meta.patternColumns: Exam.totalQuestions / totalMarks / durationMin / marksPerQ / negativeMark hold ONE paper. Where the official scheme mixes 1- and 2-mark questions (GATE, JAM) marksPerQ is 1 and negativeMark 1/3 — the true values for a 1-mark MCQ — so marksPerQ x questions != totalMarks and the score-estimate honesty gate withholds the calculator. None of these exams is in src/lib/pattern-verified.ts yet, so no answer lead / FAQ prints pattern numbers; the hub chips print the stored columns raw.

exam.name: UGC-NET — National Eligibility Test (NTA, for the University Grants Commission)
exam.description: UGC-NET is conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) for the University Grants Commission and decides eligibility for the Junior Research Fellowship (JRF), appointment as Assistant Professor and admission to PhD. December 2026 cycle: NTA's examination calendar (public notice of 16 September 2026) lists the exam for 14–19 December 2026, with 20–21 December as buffer days; NTA calls these dates tentative and says the detailed information bulletin will be issued separately — on 27 September 2026 it has not been published. Pattern as in the June 2026 information bulletin: one computer-based sitting of 3 hours with no break — Paper 1 (teaching and research aptitude) 50 questions for 100 marks and Paper 2 (the chosen subject) 100 questions for 200 marks; every question carries 2 marks and there is no negative marking. Medium: English and Hindi, except language papers. Eligibility (June 2026 bulletin): a master's degree with at least 55% marks (50% for OBC-NCL, SC, ST, PwD/PwBD and third gender candidates); final-year master's students may apply provisionally. JRF: not more than 30 years (relaxations apply); no upper age limit for Assistant Professor or PhD admission.

pattern.note: The December 2026 bulletin is not out (27 Sep 2026); the pattern is the June 2026 bulletin's.

eligibility.ageRelaxation: JRF only: not more than 30 years on the 1st day of the month in which the exam concludes; up to 5 years' relaxation for OBC-NCL, SC, ST, PwD/PwBD, third gender and women, research experience (up to 5 years), LL.M. holders (3 years) and armed-forces service; total relaxation capped at 5 years (June 2026 bulletin 3.4). No upper age limit for Assistant Professor or PhD admission.

exam.name: Joint CSIR-UGC NET (NTA, for the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research)
exam.description: Joint CSIR-UGC NET is conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) for the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research and decides eligibility for the Junior Research Fellowship (JRF), Assistant Professor and PhD admission in five subjects: Chemical Sciences; Earth, Atmospheric, Ocean and Planetary Sciences; Life Sciences; Mathematical Sciences; and Physical Sciences. December 2026 cycle: NTA's examination calendar (public notice of 16 September 2026) lists 20–21 December 2026, tentative; the information bulletin has not been published (27 September 2026). Pattern as in the June 2026 bulletin: one 3-hour computer-based paper of 200 marks in Parts A, B and C, in Hindi and English; the number of questions and the marking differ by subject. The question counts shown on this page are the Life Sciences paper's: 145 questions of which 75 are answered (Part A 15 of 20, Part B 35 of 50, Part C 25 of 75), 2, 2 and 4 marks, with 0.5, 0.5 and 1 mark deducted per wrong answer. Chemical Sciences: 120 questions, 75 answered; Earth Sciences: 150, 75; Mathematical Sciences: 120, 60 (no negative marking in Part C); Physical Sciences: 75, 55. Eligibility: a master's degree with at least 55% marks (50% for OBC-NCL, SC, ST, PwD/PwBD and third gender); JRF age limit 30 (relaxations apply), no upper age limit for Assistant Professor or PhD admission.

exam.name: CUET (PG) — Common University Entrance Test for Postgraduate Programmes (NTA)
exam.description: CUET (PG), conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA), is the entrance test for postgraduate programmes of central and other participating universities. 2027: NTA's examination calendar (public notice of 16 September 2026) lists 1–5, 8, 12–20 and 24–25 March 2027, with 30–31 March as buffer days; NTA calls these dates tentative, and the CUET (PG) 2027 information bulletin has not been published (27 September 2026). Pattern as in the CUET (PG) 2026 information bulletin: each question paper has 75 questions in 90 minutes; 4 marks for a correct answer and 1 mark deducted for a wrong one (300 marks per paper); a candidate may choose up to four question paper codes. Medium: English and Hindi, except language papers, M.Tech/Higher Sciences papers (English only) and Acharya papers. Eligibility (2026 bulletin): a bachelor's degree or equivalent, or final-year students; no age limit — each university sets its own programme eligibility.

exam.name: CLAT — Common Law Admission Test (UG), Consortium of National Law Universities
exam.description: CLAT, conducted by the Consortium of National Law Universities, is the admission test for the undergraduate (five-year integrated LLB) programmes of the participating National Law Universities. CLAT 2027 is on Sunday 6 December 2026, 2:00 pm to 4:00 pm; the online application portal is open from 3 August to 31 October 2026 (Consortium press release, 22 July 2026). UG paper: 120 multiple-choice questions of 1 mark each in 2 hours, with 0.25 mark deducted for each wrong answer — English Language 22–26 questions, Current Affairs including General Knowledge 28–32, Legal Reasoning 28–32, Logical Reasoning 22–26 and Quantitative Techniques 10–14 (approximate numbers, per the Consortium). Eligibility: 10+2 or equivalent with 45% marks (40% for SC, ST and PwD); candidates appearing in the qualifying exam in March/April 2027 may apply; no upper age limit. The postgraduate (LL.M.) exam.name: IIT JAM — Joint Admission Test for Masters (JAM 2027, IIT Kharagpur)
exam.description: JAM (Joint Admission Test for Masters) 2027 is organised by IIT Kharagpur for admission to M.Sc., M.Sc. (Tech), MS (Research), M.Sc.–M.Tech dual degree, joint M.Sc.–PhD, M.Sc.–PhD dual degree and integrated PhD programmes at the IITs and other institutes; the JAM 2027 site lists 3,000 seats. One computer-based exam on Sunday 14 February 2027 in two sessions — forenoon 9:30–12:30: Chemistry, Geology, Mathematics; afternoon 2:30–5:30: Biotechnology, Economics, Mathematical Statistics, Physics. A candidate may take one paper, or two in different sessions. Every paper: 60 questions, 100 marks, 3 hours — Section A 30 multiple-choice questions (one-third of a mark deducted for a wrong 1-mark answer and two-thirds for a wrong 2-mark answer), Section B 10 multiple-select questions and Section C 20 numerical-answer questions, with no negative marking in B or C. Applications 11 September – 19 October 2026; results 18 March 2027. Eligibility: an undergraduate degree, or appearing in its final examination in 2027; open to all nationals, no age restriction.

Paper-II: 100 questions for 300 marks in 2 hours on the chosen engineering part, 1 mark deducted per wrong answer. Questions in Hindi and English. exam.name: SSC CPO — Sub-Inspector in Delhi Police and Central Armed Police Forces Examination (Staff Selection Commission)
exam.description: The Staff Selection Commission's Sub-Inspector in Delhi Police and Central Armed Police Forces Examination 2026 (SSC CPO) recruits Sub-Inspectors (Executive) in Delhi Police, Sub-Inspectors (GD) in the CAPFs and Sub-Inspectors (Fire) in the CISF — Level-6 (Rs 35,400–1,12,400). Notice of 10 September 2026: apply online by 30 September 2026 (23:00), fee by 1 October 2026; correction window 8–10 October 2026; the computer-based exam date is 'to be notified later'. Stages: Paper-I, physical standard and endurance tests, Paper-II and a medical examination. Paper-I: 100 questions for 100 marks in 1 hour (15-minute sectional timer) — General Intelligence and Reasoning, General Knowledge and General Awareness, Quantitative Aptitude and English Comprehension, 25 each — with 0.25 deducted per wrong answer. Paper-II: General Intelligence and Reasoning, General Knowledge and General Awareness, and Quantitative Aptitude, 20 questions for 40 marks each, in 1 hour (20-minute sectional timer), and English Comprehension, 100 questions for 200 marks, in 1 hour — with 0.50 deducted per wrong answer. Parts I–III of both papers are set in Hindi and English. Age 20–25 on 1 August 2026 (18–30 for SI Fire in CISF), relaxations apply. Education: a bachelor's degree (SI Fire: B.Sc. with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, or matriculation plus a three-year engineering diploma).

exam.name: BITSAT — BITS Admission Test (BITS Pilani)
exam.description: BITSAT is BITS Pilani's computer-based admission test for its first-degree programmes (B.E., M.Sc. and B.Pharm.). BITSAT-2027 dates are not announced: on 27 September 2026 the admissions site says the 2026–27 admission cycle is closed. Pattern as in the BITSAT-2026 brochure: one 3-hour sitting with no break, 130 multiple-choice questions — Physics 30, Chemistry 30, English Proficiency 10, Logical Reasoning 20, and Mathematics or Biology 40 — with 3 marks for a correct answer and 1 deducted for a wrong one; a candidate who answers all 130 may attempt 12 extra questions. Questions and instructions are in English only. A candidate may sit up to two sessions; the higher score counts. Eligibility (2026): 12th under the 10+2 system with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics (or Biology, for B.Pharm., B.E. Environmental and Sustainability Engineering and M.Sc. Biological Sciences), at least 75% aggregate in those three subjects and 60% in each.

pattern.quote: Each session of BITSAT-2026 will be of 3 hours duration (without break) … Each correct answer fetches 3 marks, while each incorrect answer has a penalty of 1 mark (-1 mark). … There will be 130 questions in all … Part I Physics 30; Part II Chemistry 30; Part III (a) English Proficiency 10 (b) Logical Reasoning 20; Part IV Mathematics … OR Biology … 40; Total 130. … If a candidate answers all the 130 questions … option of attempting 12 (twelve) extra questions … All the questions and instructions of the test will be in English only.
pattern.note: 390 = 130 x 3 (arithmetic on the brochure's figures); the 12 optional extra questions are not in the stored count.

eligibility.educationNote: 12th (10+2) with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics (or Biology for B.Pharm., B.E. Environmental and Sustainability Engg. and M.Sc. Biological Sciences): at least 75% aggregate in those three subjects and 60% in each (BITSAT-2026 rules).

exam.name: JNVST — Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya Selection Test, Class VI (Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti)
exam.description: The Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya Selection Test (JNVST) is Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti's admission test for Class VI in the Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas — co-educational residential schools with free education, board and lodging. JNVST 2027 (for the 2027-28 session) is on 28 November 2026, 11:30 am to 1:30 pm, in a single phase; NVS expects to announce results by the end of March 2027. The test: 80 objective questions for 100 marks in 2 hours on an OMR sheet — Mental Ability Test and Environmental Studies 40 questions (50 marks, 60 minutes), Arithmetic 20 (25 marks, 30 minutes) and Language 20 (25 marks, 30 minutes); 1.25 marks per correct answer and no negative marking. It is held in the languages listed for each state. Eligibility: bona fide residents of the district studying in Class V in 2026-27 at a recognised school, born between 1 May 2015 and 31 July 2017 (both inclusive), who studied a full session in each of Classes III, IV and V.

pattern.quote: 5. Composition of the Selection Test — The selection test will be of two-hour duration from 11:30 AM to 01:30 PM and will have 3 sections with only objective type questions. There are 80 questions in all for 100 marks. Mental ability Test and Environmental Studies (EVS) 20 + 20, 25 + 25, 60 Minutes; Arithmetic Test 20, 25, 30 Minutes; Language Test 20, 25, 30 Minutes … e) 1.25 marks will be given for every correct answer. f) No negative marking will be done.
pattern.note: languages = the prospectus's state-wise list (section 4) restricted to the ten the Language enum holds; Urdu, Odia, Assamese and others are also offered in some states.
